patients.label: 23-year-old male healthcare professional with mask-related chronic postauricular and scalp dermatitis

identity_evidence.quote: We report a case of a 23-year-old male healthcare professional

attribution_limitations: The authors state that continuous friction, prolonged topical corticosteroid exposure and abrupt tapering likely precipitated barrier compromise and secondary seborrheic inflammation; this is author speculation and is not recorded as a fact.

The same-time order of corticosteroid taper, tacrolimus/fusidic acid and the later management paragraph relative to each other is only partly stated; the final management regimen (low-potency corticosteroids, emollients, education) is not dated and its start relative to the seborrheic stage is not stated.
The source states laboratory evaluation was not indicated because the diagnosis was made clinically; no laboratory test or result is reported.

evidence.quote:
Figure 1
Initial presentation showing a well-demarcated erythematous and scaly plaque in the right postauricular region following prolonged mask use.

Figure 2
Clinical progression showing extension of the lesion into the adjacent scalp with greasy scaling and crust formation, findings consistent with seborrheic-type inflammation.

Figure 3
Partial response after treatment, showing residual erythema and scaling following intermittent topical corticosteroid therapy and barrier-repair measures.

limitations: Figure visual status in this annotation stays not_inspected; the three clinical photographs were viewed separately in the visual submission.
No dates, calendar times, laboratory values or follow-up duration are reported; times are relative only.
Figure 3 caption (partial response) and the text callout for Figure 3 (chronic seborrheic stage) describe different stages; both are recorded as written.
Discussion sentences about cited literature are background and not patient facts.

The text callout for Figure 2 sits at the partial recurrence after tapering (persistent erythema and scaling), while the Figure 2 caption describes scalp extension with greasy scaling and crust; greasy quality and crust are not resolvable in the pixels. Both kept as written.

claims.text: A 23-year-old male healthcare professional developed erythematous and pruritic plaques in the right postauricular region about three weeks after continuous mask use during the COVID-19 pandemic. Examination showed erythematous scaly plaques extending from the retroauricular fold into the adjacent scalp and external auditory canal, consistent with early irritant contact dermatitis. He had no history of atopic dermatitis, psoriasis or seborrheic dermatitis, no new hair or skin products, and no systemic symptoms; psoriasis, allergic contact dermatitis and superficial fungal infection were considered and excluded, and laboratory evaluation was not indicated.
